title: In-Orbit Processing or Not? Sunlight-Aware Task Scheduling for Energy-Efficient Space Edge Computing Networks
authors: Weisen Liu; Zeqi Lai; Qian Wu; Hewu Li; Qi Zhang; Zonglun Li; Yuanjie Li; Jun Liu

problem_statement.en: Space edge computing (SEC) faces significant energy constraints due to the additional power consumption of on-board hardware, which negatively impacts battery lifetime and task execution. Naive offloading to ground stations can overwhelm downlinks and introduce unacceptable latency for time-sensitive tasks.
problem_statement.zh: 太空邊緣計算（SEC）面臨顯著的能源限制，星載硬體的額外功耗會縮短電池壽命並影響任務執行；而簡單地將任務卸載至地面站可能導致下行鏈路擁塞，並對時間敏感任務引入難以接受的延遲。

key_innovation.en: PHOENIX, a sunlight-aware task scheduling framework that dynamically offloads space tasks to 'sunlight-sufficient' edges (satellites with near-100% sunlit ratio) or ground stations to minimize battery depth-of-discharge (DoD) while meeting task deadlines.
key_innovation.zh: PHOENIX 是一套日照感知任務 scheduling 框架，動態地將太空任務卸載至「日照充足」的邊緣節點（日照率接近 100% 的衛星）或地面站，以最小化電池放電深度（DoD），同時滿足任務截止時間要求。

key_improvements.en: Reduces maximum battery DoD by up to 54.8% and prolongs battery lifetime to 2.9x compared to state-of-the-art solutions.
key_improvements.zh: 相較於現有最優方案，最大電池放電深度最高降低 54.8%，電池壽命延長至 2.9x。
